## Summary

US animal protection group (now Humane World for Animals); ACE evaluated its Farm Animal Protection Campaign. Animal Charity Evaluators published one public model of its work. The most recent, from November 2016, puts it at **37 animals spared per dollar** as the evaluator published it, with our default exchange rates between units.

This page reproduces the evaluator's own spreadsheet. We haven't yet written our own evaluation of this charity, so there is no charityevals view: the numbers are the evaluator's.

## The models

| Model | By | Date | Result | Cells reproduced |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [HSUS Farm Animal Protection Campaign: 2016 estimate (ACE)](/humane-society-of-the-united-states) | ACE | November 2016 | 37 animals spared per dollar | 0 |

Grants, renewals and research grants each came with their own spreadsheet, so a charity can have several models of the same program, years apart. The rankings use the most recent.

## How this was imported

The Guesstimate model was converted cell by cell. Its inputs are 90% intervals, used here as low and high values with the median as the best guess. Guesstimate itself shows Monte Carlo means, which run higher when inputs are skewed, so the central figure here is lower than Guesstimate's.

## What's not here yet

- The evaluator's moral weights and discount rates are fixed in these models, so changing your assumptions doesn't move them.
- Only the ranges ACE gave are varied; correlations between them aren't modelled.
- A hand-written evaluation: what the program does, what the evidence says and where the model is most uncertain.
